subject: Estimating the parameters of the von mises distribution in stan

messages.author: 199e2eb8726aba5e
messages.subject: Estimating the parameters of the von mises distribution in stan
parts:
Hi! I am new to stan and trying to get a model up and running in stan, it would be a great addition to my PhD. However, I am having a little trouble with the von mises distribution, namely estimating the parameters.

First I simulate some data in R (using circular package).
out <- rvonmises(n=100, circular(pi, modulo = '2pi'), 30)

Then I execute the following stan code:

data{
int N;
vector[N] out;
}

parameters{
real mu;
real<lower=0> kappa;
}

model{
mu ~ normal(pi(),1);
kappa ~exponential(0.05);

out ~ von_mises(mu, kappa);

}

fit <- stan(file = 'vonmises_test.stan', data=list(N=100, out=out), chains=4)

This is the result.
           mean se_mean      sd      2.5%       25%       50%       75%     97.5% n_eff      Rhat
mu      1.56831 1.92320 2.72054  -3.16661   1.53197   3.12989   3.14703   3.17394     2 151.83486
kappa  28.64963 0.06479 3.93674  21.66592  25.88408  28.48742  31.21542  36.94496  3691   0.99966
lp__  205.59226 6.04681 8.59502 189.46066 199.60578 210.41353 211.08583 211.49364     2   9.46877

The output for the parameter mu changes somewhat randomly! I am not quite sure what I am doing wrong here!


Thank you in advance for your assistance.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Estimating the parameters of the von mises distribution in stan
parts:
On Thursday, April 27, 2017 at 3:14:56 PM UTC-4, T the stressed Phd wrote:
I am not quite sure what I am doing wrong here!

What you had wasn't really wrong; it just didn't give the right answer. First, you don't want kappa to be too close to zero or HMC will have problems. To do that, you can write your code like this

data{
  int<lower=0> N;
  vector[N] out;
  real<lower=0> rate;
}
transformed data {
  real<lower=0> scale = 1 / rate;
}
parameters{
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> kappa_unscaled;
}
transformed parameters {
  real kappa = scale * kappa_unscaled;
}
model{
  mu ~ normal(pi(),1);
  kappa_unscaled ~ exponential(1);
  out ~ von_mises(mu, kappa);
}

which implies that your beliefs about kappa (before seeing the data) are exponential with the rate passed to the data block. Then, it seems necessary for you to shrink the starting values in order to get it to work reliably for all of the chains, using for example:

fit <- stan(file = 'vonmises.stan', data=list(N=100, out=out, rate = .05), chains=4, init_r=.1)

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Estimating the parameters of the von mises distribution in stan
parts:
On Friday, April 28, 2017 at 6:58:55 PM UTC-4, T the stressed Phd wrote:
Is there any more suggestions for this? If this is the case when we know the correct value, is it thus not robust to using the von mises distribution in stan for real data where we have no intuition for the true values of the distribution?

Lots of things can go wrong, but when they do it should be apparent in the results. In this case, it shows up as lack of convergence. In other situations, the problem could be divergent transitions or low Bayesian Fraction of Missing Information. Just pay attention to any warnings you see, except for the irrelevant ones.

Ben
